caseno: Writ Petition Nos. 5458, 5459 with No. 5872 of 2004.
lawyer:
Mahmudul lslam with Mizanul Haque Chowdhury and Md Hasan Rajib Prodhan, Advocates------ For the Petitioners. 
M Fida Kamal. Attorney General with Nahid Mahtab, Deputy Attorney-General------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Abdul Baten (Md) ------ Petitioner
vs
Chairman, NBR & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: In the above Rules Nisi, a declaration that levy and collection of advance VAT at the rate of 1.5% ad-valorem pursuant to the notification being SRO No. 260 dated 30-8-04 was not applicable in the cases of the petitioners who were as registered commercial importers and traders paying and intending to pay trading VAT at supply stage as per-provisions of the first proviso to section 5(2) and section 9 of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991, briefly, the VAT Act, on the basis of the value addition were sought for.

2. In Writ Petition No. 5458 of 2004 the petitioner is stated to be a proprietor and registered importer. He is engaged in the business of import or sugar from various countries on the basis of licence. In the course of business, he opened on 6-7-04 a letter of credit for import of 15,000 metric tons of white sugar of Brazilian origin at the rate of US$ 182.50 per metric ton under HS Code No. 1701.11.00. After arrival of the goods at the Chittagong port, six bills of entry namely C-211450, C-211530, C-211284, C-211543, C-211553 and C-211257 all dated 29.08.04 were submitted for clearance of the goods. Respondent No.2, the Commissioner of Customs assessed said sugar to duty at the rate of US$ 216 per metricton. Against said assessment, the petitioner moved this division in Writ petition No. 5244 of 2004 and obtained a Rule Nisi and also an ad-interim order of release on payment of the duties and other charges on the basis of the invoice value in cash and furnishing bank guarantee for the disputed duties and taxes.

3. It is further stated that the petitioner is a commercial importer and paid VAT at the rate of 15% at the stage of import and also is paying VAT at the supply stage for longtime on the basis of approved price list. The petitioner had to pay Taka 17,80,116.00 more as advance VAT at the rate of 1.5% ad-valorem of said imported goods cleared by aforesaid bills of entry by furnishing a bank guarantee on the basis of an ad-interim order pending disposal of the Rule.

4. In Writ Petition No. 5459 of 2004, the same petitioner imported 5,000 metric tons of white sugar of Brazilian origin at the rate of US$ 182.50 per metric ton under the same HS 'Code No. 1701.11.00 by opening a letter of credit dated 22-4-04. After arrival of the goods at the Chittagong port, four bills of entry, namely, C-211367, C-211484, C-211442 and C-211233 all dated 29-8-04 were submitted for clearance of said sugar. The Customs Authority assessed the goods to duty at the rate of US $ 216 per metric ton.

5. Being aggrieved, similarly, the petitioner obtained a Rule in Writ Petition No. 5243 of 2004 and an ad interim order of release of the consignment on payment of duties and taxes on the basis of invoice value in cash and on furnishing bank guarantee for the rest of duties and taxes levied. And the petitioner again obtained the present Rule and an ad-interim order of release of the goods by furnishing bank guarantee in respect of the payment of advance VAT only.

6. In the Writ Petition No. 5872 of 2004 another petitioner in similar situation imported 6,000 metric tons of white sugar of Thai Origin at the rate of USS .185.00 per metric ton under same Code No. 1701.11.00 by opening a letter of credit dated 23-8-2004.

7. After arrival of said sugar at the Chittagong port, three bills of entry, namely, C-261748, C- 261776 and C-261784 all dated 21-10-04 were submitted for clearance of the goods. But the Customs Authority assessed said goods to duty at the rate of USS 224 per metric ton:

8. Being aggrieved, the petitioner obtained a Rule in a writ petition and an ad-interim order of release on payment of the duties and taxes at the rate of invoice value in cash and rest of the duties and taxes by way of furnishing bank guarantee. When the custom authority further demanded advance VAT at the rate of 1.5% the petitioner obtained the present Rule and ultimately got release of the goods by furnishing bank guarantee for an amount of Taka 18,83,376 for advance VAT.

9. Affidavit of facts in all the writ petitions were filed on behalf of respondent No.3, the Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT. In the affidavit, copies of an order dated 10-8-04 regarding payment of advance VAT at the time of import and the Notification being SRO No. 172 dated 11-6-04 imposing advance VAT at the rate of 10% are annexed as Annexures-1 and 2. In the affidavit, the circumstances are stated for levy and collection of advance VAT from a commercial importer at the time of import.

10. The petitioners also filed supplementary affidavit annexing copies of the bank guarantees submitted pursuant to the ad-interim direction for release of the imported goods, declaration of the price for approval by the concerned VAT authorities and approval of the price declared and the certificates of payment of VAT at the trading stage of the goods imported against respective bills or entry as Annexure I, J, K and L.

11. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Advocate took us through the Notification being SRO No. 143 dated 10-6-2001. Notification being SRO No.172 dated 10-6-2004 and Notification being SRO No. 260 dated 30-8-2004.and submitted that in view of sub-section 2 of section 5 the petitioners as both commercial importer and trader have been paying VAT at the rate of 15% at the time of import and again at the same rate of 15% on the price of goods as approved by the VAT authorities at the trading stage and taking rebate under section 9 of the VAT Act, levy and collection of the advance VAT at the time of import of the goods was not applicable to the cases of the petitioners.

12. He also submitted that in view of the option pursuant to the proviso to paragraph 2 of the Notification being SRO No. 172 dated 10-6-2004 exercised by the petitioners, the VAT authorities could not force the petitioners to pay advance trading tax at the time of import and the advance trading tax what was collected at the time of import against the aforesaid bills of entry by way of bank guarantee is now liable to be refunded to the petitioners.

13. Mr M Fida Kamal, Attorney-General, submitted that introduction and collection of advance VAT at the time of import became necessary because of the facts that after import in many cases neither the imported goods nor the importer could be traced out for payment of the VAT at trading or supply stage.

14. He also submitted that the importer who paid advance VAT at the time of import shall be entitled to get proportionate return of said VAT on proof of payment of VAT as determined by the VAT authorities at the trading or supply stage against the bill of entry of the goods cleared in accordance with law.

15. We have perused the records. As the questions raised in the writ petitions are the same, we heard them together and now, dispose of them by this order. Only issue raised in the writ petitions is whether or not levy and collection of advance VAT at the rate of 1.5 percent from the petitioners who ate both commercial importer and trader were lawful and authorised.

16. In order to appreciate the submissions of learned Advocates we examined the aforesaid Notifications in the light of relevant provisions of the VAT Act.

17. Section 5 of the VAT Act provides inter alia the methods for determination of the value of goods upon which VAT is 10 be paid at the time of import and supply, the rate of VAT payable at the time of sale, exchange or transfer of the goods manufactured or imported upon the value on which the rebate is obtained and also empowers the National Board of Revenue to fix by gazette notification the amount and rate of value addition in order to determine the basis of VAT.

18. Thus empowered, National Board of Revenue issued the Notification being SRO No. 143-Law/2001/308-Musuk dated 7-6-2001 fixing the rate of value addition at 10 percent subject to certain terms and conditions for the purpose of payment of VAT at the rate of 1.5 percent by the traders (ব্যবসায়ী). Then, the National Board of Revenue issued the Notification being SRO No. 172-Law/2004/418-VAT dated 10-6-2004 superseding earlier Notification but maintaining said rate of value addition and fixing minimum VAT payable monthly/yearly by the retailers and others subject to certain conditions, The National Board of Revenue then issued the Notification being SRO No. 260-law/2004-431-VAT dated 30-8-2004 for payment in advance of said VAT of 1.5% what is payable at the trading or supply stage by the commercial importer at the time of import against the bill of entry on the assessable value plus customs duty, and supplementary duty and development surcharge, if any, plus value addition at the rate of 10 percent.

19. In the conditions provided under paragraph 2 of the Notification dated 10-6-2004 a detailed procedure is prescribed for the traders who want to pay VAT at the rate of 1.5 percent on the value addition at the rate of 10 percent of the goods imported or collected (সংগহীত) at the time of supply. Close reading of the Notifications makes it clear that an option is given to the commercial importers who are not manufacturers or traders and have not availed the opportunity as traders for payment of VAT at the supply stage pursuant to the Notification dated 10-6-2004 to pay VAT in advance at the rate of 1.5 percent at the time of import of goods as per the Notification dated 30-8-2005. Mr Mahmudul Islam did not challenge the vires of the Notification but claimed that such payment of VAT at the rate or 1.5 percent in advance is not applicable in the cases of the petitioners, who were registered both as Commercial importer and traders have been paying VAT at the rate of said 1.5 percent on the value addition at the time of supply and got rebate of the input tax.

20. It is the case of the petitioners that they as commercial importer paid requisite VAT at the time of import of the goods against aforesaid bills of entry and then, got the price of the goods approved by the concerned VAT authority and paid as traders the amount of VAT at the rate of 1.5 percent on the value addition at the supply stage of the goods and received the rebate of the input tax against the goods cleared against respective bills of entry.

21. It is also not disputed that the petitioners paid Taka 17,80,116.00, Taka 15,49,656.00 and Taka 18,83,376.00 as advance VAT at the rate of 1.5 percent pursuant to the Notification being SRO No. 260 dated 30-8-2004 at the time of import of said goods. Copies of the certificates from the relevant VAT authority annexed as Annexure L to the supplementary affidavits evidence payment of trading VAT of Taka 22,22,590.42 in respect of the goods cleared by two bills of entry being C-211257 and C-0211543 dated 29-8-2004 in Writ Petition No. 5458, Taka 25,50,094.58 in respect of goods cleared by four bills of entry being C-211484, C-211361, C- 211233 and C-211442 dated 29-8-2004 in Writ Petition No. 5459 of 2004 and Taka 25,80,756.63 in respect of goods cleared by three bills of entry being C-261748, C-261716 and C-261784 all dated 21-10-2004 in Writ Petition No. 5872 of 2004.

<u>22. In view of the payment of trading VAT more than the amount of the advance VAT determined and secured by the bank guarantees at the time of import of said goods, there is now no difficulty for the VAT authorities, which was readily conceded to by Mrs Nahid Mahtab, to return the bank guarantees to the petitioners. In the aforesaid circumstances, the petitioners as registered commercial importers and traders having paid trading VAT were not required to pay advance VAT at the time of import of said goods.</u>

In the result, the Rules are made absolute without any order as to cost. The concerned Commissioner is accordingly, directed to return the bank guarantees received in the above Writ Petitions to the respective petitioners within a period of one month of receipt of this order, positively.

End.
